ety.text: From люлю (ljulju), an interjection used to lull babies. Compare to English lull, Swedish lulla (“to lull”), Icelandic lúlla (“to lull”).
From Turkic (Ottoman Turkish لوله (lüle)), ultimately from Persian لوله (lule).
First attested in 1992. From English Pampers, a genericized trademark brand of diapers, from English pamper.
Calque of translingual Hipposideridae, from the plural of подковогу́бый (podkovogúbyj), from подковогу́б (podkovogúb).
пол- (pol-, “half”) + ночь (nočʹ, “night”), with ночь (nočʹ) placed in the genitive case.

From Old Church Slavonic простълюдинъ (prostŭljudinŭ), from про́стъ (próstŭ, “simple, ordinary”) and людинъ (ljudinŭ, “free man”); see просто́й (prostój) and лю́ди (ljúdi). Compare with Ukrainian просто́люд (prostóljud, “commoners (collective)”).
Reinterpretation of the word пугу́ч (pugúč), compare onomatopoeic пу́гу́ (púgú, “the sound made by an eagle owl”).
Borrowed from Greek σκουμπριά (skoumpriá), plural of σκουμπρί (skoumprí).
